- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate when true values show strong upward momentum; adjust upward if recent history shows rising trend.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak or use moving average smoothing.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is consistently above true values, reduce by 5–10% of the deviation; if below, increase by similar margin.
- Lagged response: if true values rise after forecast, delay peak forecast by 1–2 periods; if true falls after forecast, anticipate drop 1–2 periods ahead.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 5–7 days dominate forecast, reduce weight or apply decay factor to older data.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers (e.g., >15% above or below mean); cap or clip forecasts to historical 95% confidence band.
